subject: C22
required_fixes: C22-R2-F1 (high): Preserve interrupted remote-call evidence even when no engine export exists. crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:466 initializes latest from restore, so a new conversation has None; start() at :1019-1043 obtains no initial export, and HistoryRead is requested only after end_turn (:1923-1929). The stop-time save at :566 requires Some(export). Thus, approve an MCP call during the first turn and sleep/quit/end while the server is running it: final cleanup marks its entry interrupted in memory (:605-612), but no protected record is saved and no save failure is reported. Relaunch loses the evidence of a call that may have executed. The same gate affects a later interrupted turn after an export failure leaves latest absent. This leaves D049/T23 uncertain-outcome preservation incomplete. Persist the transcript/outcome independently of replay availability, or establish a valid checkpoint before dispatch; absence of a valid export must prevent continuation rather than erase the record or fabricate restore context. Acceptance: with no preceding completed turn, admit an actual delayed MCP call, stop after dispatch, relaunch offline and read the protected interrupted/unknown call record; reconnect and explicit recovery must not replay it. Also cover the no-export branch after export refusal.
evidence_gaps: C22-R2-G1: The submitted interrupted-call T23 test at crates/desktop-core/tests/workspace_mcp/main.rs:940-956 first completes 'Hello.', waits for savedAt, and captures its history ID. It establishes preservation only with a prior export. Add source-bound production-interface evidence for the no-export cases in C22-R2-F1, with server-side dispatch/execution evidence, offline inspection, and no replay on reconnect. Other parts of the earlier G1 are covered; combined rotation G2 and trace correlation G3 are supported.
optional_suggestions: In signing_out_during_a_sign_in_again_never_signs_the_server_back_in, replace the 300 ms assumption with an observable token-exchange gate and assert revocation of the specific late-issued tokens. The current final 'any mcp-refresh' assertion can be satisfied by revoking the pre-existing sign-in. Source flow checks support the fix; this would make its race evidence more precise.

The remaining defect is established from the production control flow and test preconditions, not a newly executed runtime reproduction. Only this designated verdict artifact is written.
